newsitem.title: ITALY: European truckers to hold protest in Milan.
newsitem.headline: European truckers to hold protest in Milan.

text.p: European truckers, in solidarity with striking French colleagues, will meet in Milan on Monday after a protest drive through the city centre, the Italian road transport federation FAI said on Thursday.

A FAI spokeswoman said 12 trucks will set off from Piazzale Loreto and drive slowly to Corso Venezia, both central city locations, where truckers' leaders will discuss their main demand for a cut in diesel prices for the sector.
Traffic was likely to be severely disrupted, she said.

It will be the first meeting in Italy of truckers' federations from France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain and Italy to set a common platform of demands for government and European Union action to aid the sector, the spokeswoman said.

The Milan meeting had been fixed on November 7 when European truckers protested in Brussels for a fuel rebate and before the pay strike by French drivers who voted on Thursday to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy.

Milan's Piazzale Loreto, a traditional rallying point for Italian trades unions, is where Mussolini, his mistress Claretta Petacci and other fascist leaders were strung up after being executed by partisans on April 28, 1945.
